title: Cardinal saturation and elementary-map homogeneity

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory (2017 course; revised July 13, 2021)

summary: Realize types over small parameter sets and extend specified elementary maps, using cardinal bounds that remain valid at singular cardinals.
abstract: An elementary correspondence between a few points can be extended by realizing the description of one more point. Cardinal saturation makes the same method available when the old domain is infinite but smaller than a chosen cardinal. We prove the exact one-point extension, then count the points added in a transfinite construction. When both structures have the matching size bound, requests from both sides produce an isomorphism extending every prescribed old value, and self-maps extend to automorphisms. The counting argument works at singular cardinals as well; realization of types and construction of saturated models of a prescribed size are kept distinct.
